doc: The control plane's read model: the routing table, the tasks mirrored from the code host, the run records and the audit log.

glossary.meaning: The founder-owned table saying which model fills each tier and which tier takes each job
One tier of the routing table and the model that fills it
One job kind of the routing table and the tier that takes it
A task issue on the code host, read with its state, risk and kind
Where a task stands, from the issue's state label
What the runner records about one attempt at a task: the tier, the routing row that chose it, the model used and the outcome
How a run ended, or running while it has not
One line of the append-only audit log: who did what to which subject, and when
A secret or an API token as the control plane may show it: its name, dates and state, never its value
Why the daily credential-expiry check reports a credential: its reminder date has come, or it has expired
One line of the credential-expiry check: a credential's kind, name, state and expiry date, never a value

functions.name: routing_view
rules: Returns the same routing with the tiers sorted by tier name and the jobs sorted by job name
Does not change its argument

functions.name: task_from_issue

params.name: labels
params.doc: In the order the code host lists them

rules: The state comes from the labels that start with state: ; the part after the colon, with hyphens read as underscores, must be a TaskState other than unlabelled and conflict, or the label is ignored
One such label gives that state, none gives unlabelled, more than one gives conflict
The risk is the part after risk: of the first label that starts with it, and the kind likewise after kind: ; empty when there is none
The number, title and milestone are copied

functions.name: page_size
functions.doc: How many items a list returns
rules: Returns 50 when limit is 0 or negative
Returns 200 when limit is above 200
Otherwise returns limit

functions.name: credentials_of_kind
functions.doc: The secrets or the tokens of a credential list
rules: Returns the credentials whose kind is the given one, in their order
Returns an empty list, not nothing, when there are none
Does not change its argument

functions.name: credential_problem
functions.doc: Whether a credential's name and dates are acceptable
rules: A name is acceptable when it has 1 to 100 characters, each a printable ASCII character other than a space
A date is acceptable when it is empty or a real calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD
A reminder is acceptable when it is not after the expiry; with no expiry any acceptable reminder is
Returns an empty string when the name and both dates are acceptable; otherwise a short sentence for the first problem, in the order name, expiry, reminder, reminder against expiry
The sentence never repeats the name or a date

functions.name: credential_alerts
functions.doc: What the daily credential-expiry check reports
rules: Skips a revoked credential and one with no expires_on
A credential is expired when its expires_on is before today (a token is refused from the day after)
Otherwise it is remind when its remind_on is today or earlier or, with no remind_on, its expires_on is within 30 days of today
Any other credential is not reported
Each alert carries the credential's kind, name and expires_on, never anything else
Returns the alerts soonest expires_on first, then by kind, then by name; an empty list, not nothing, when there are none
Does not change its argument
